text.p: These are the stories making headlines in the Namibian newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
* Despite disruption of the crowning ceremony by police and gunmen, Jonas Shikulya was installed as king of the Aadhimba at Ruacana over the weekend.

* Plans are underway to make the directorate of elections and the electoral commission independent of government, a move which the opposition DTA of Namibia hopes will take place before the December local elections.

* The DTA has sharply criticised what it terms the arbitrary leadership of Namibian president Sam Nujoma. In a statement released following the party's central committee meeting over the weekend, the DTA expresses dissatisfaction with the president more and more often ruling by decree, instead of adhering to the laws of the country passed by parliament.
* In the seven years since independence Telecom Namibia has more than doubled the number of its customers.
* The DTA has reshuffled its top structure and has decided to fill its vacancy in the national assembly with an "outsider".
* The ostrich industry is facing its darkest hours following an average drop of 33 percent in prices paid to farmers, who deliver to Ostraco, the ostrich abattoir outside Mariental.

* President Sam Nujoma has urged developing countries to introduce the concept of Zero Emissions to help combat desertification. He was speaking at the annual world congress on zero emissions in Indonesia on Friday.
